routes.description: Establish that Iraq's exceptional conduct made intervention defensible despite its costs, while showing that morality and political judgment do not require divine authority and can be corrupted by religious command, institutions, or absolutism.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds by supplying a principled basis for overriding Iraqi sovereignty, connecting removal to defensible ends, grounding moral agency independently of revelation, and explaining how asserted divine authority can distort conduct or obstruct peaceful political settlement.

motionBridge.description: Show both that intervention in Iraq met a defensible exception to restraint and that religion can corrupt rather than uniquely supply moral authority.

centralBridges.description: Identify regime conduct serious enough to defeat the ordinary presumption of sovereignty and nonintervention.
Connect regime removal and post-invasion consequences to humanitarian or strategic ends capable of answering foreseeable costs.
Explain how truth, solidarity, and moral responsibility can operate without commands from a personal deity.
Show mechanisms by which divine authorization, absolutism, or religious institutions can license harm or impede revisable judgment.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Challenge the evidentiary passage from cosmic origins or order to a personal, morally authoritative deity.
Distinguish harms caused by secular humanism from harms merely committed by regimes carrying atheist or anti-clerical labels.

routes.description: Establish that the Iraq invasion lacked a coherent justification sufficient to overcome its foreseeable human and strategic costs, while showing that transcendent authority grounds objective moral obligation and that religion's abuses do not negate its moral and civilizational functions.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds by maintaining the moral distinction between aggression and restraint, demonstrating an adverse or inconsistent intervention rationale, explaining why secular preference cannot bind moral duty, and answering claims that religious belief uniquely causes cruelty or tyranny.

motionBridge.description: Show both that the Iraq invasion failed the burden for justified war and that religion can supply indispensable moral authority despite misuse.

centralBridges.description: Require a coherent and sufficiently exceptional justification before aggressive war may override sovereignty and the presumption of restraint.
Account for civilian, military, fiscal, strategic, and moral consequences when testing whether intervention was defensible.
Explain why recognition of moral rules requires an authority beyond individual or collective preference to become binding.
Show how religious belief can redirect destructive impulses, support self-government, and sustain moral or civilizational order despite human misuse.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Defend contested religious narratives by distinguishing their governing lesson from the harmful act represented within them.
Use avowedly anti-religious persecution to test claims that removing religious authority reliably prevents absolutism or political cruelty.

sections.title: Sovereignty, Aggression, and the Case for Intervention
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether Saddam Hussein's conduct created a principled exception to sovereignty and whether intervention and nonintervention bear materially different moral burdens.

sections.title: Consequences and Strategic Balance in Iraq
sections.rationale: The defensibility of intervention also turns on its anticipated and realized human, fiscal, regional, humanitarian, and institutional consequences.

sections.title: From Cosmic Order to Divine Moral Authority
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether arguments from origin, order, or design warrant belief in a personal deity capable of grounding authoritative moral requirements.

sections.title: Secular Moral Agency and Transcendent Obligation
sections.rationale: The central moral-authority clash concerns whether solidarity and reason can ground responsible conduct or whether binding obligation requires a transcendent source.

sections.title: Religious Command, Redemption, and Practical Harm
sections.rationale: Contested doctrines and examples reveal whether religious authority restrains destructive impulses or instead licenses submission, transferred guilt, absolutism, and political obstruction.

sections.title: Religion, Atheism, and Political Tyranny
sections.rationale: Historical disputes over fascist, communist, clerical, and anti-clerical power test the claimed causal relationship between religious or secular commitments and organized persecution.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-02.proposition: Saddam Hussein's regime made removal defensible by committing mass atrocities and regional aggression while supporting terrorism and pursuing catastrophic weapons capabilities.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-03.proposition: A recovered federal Iraq could benefit Iraqis, diversify control of vital oil resources, and constrain the regional influence of the Iranian and Saudi theocracies.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-04.proposition: Intervention produced concrete gains through prosecution of Saddam's leadership, restoration of the southern marshes, Kurdish autonomy, and flourishing civil society in northern Iraq.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-06.proposition: Iraq forfeited ordinary sovereignty through genocide, prohibited weapons, support for international terrorism, and repeated aggression against neighboring states.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-07.proposition: Even granting a possible first cause or prime mover, no adequate reasoned path establishes a personal deity that supervises conduct and answers prayers.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-09.proposition: Religion diminishes human moral integrity by claiming that people cannot recognize or choose right action without permission and instruction from a celestial authority.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: Vicarious redemption is immoral because guilt and moral responsibility cannot legitimately be transferred from a wrongdoer to an innocent sacrificial substitute.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: The universe's accelerating expansion, eventual desolation, and pervasive suffering count against claims that it reflects competent and benevolent design.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Invoking divine authorization does not cure nihilism or relativism but can grant perpetrators unlimited moral permission and intensify cruelty.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: Human solidarity and ordinary decency arise naturally without religious command, while enlightened self-interest can reinforce concern for other people's welfare.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-09.proposition: Twentieth-century totalitarian crimes do not show that rational atheism causes tyranny because fascism allied with churches and communist regimes reproduced religious structures of worship and servility.

chunk-004:chunk-004-candidate-02.proposition: A valid indictment of secular humanism requires an example of a state adopting humanist teachings and consequently descending into massacre and tyranny because of those teachings.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-01.proposition: The Iraq invasion was an arrogant and self-righteous idealist undertaking whose foreseeable folly supplied inadequate grounds for war and made it both wrong and a strategic mistake.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-05.proposition: The invasion produced immense financial, human, strategic, and moral costs, strengthened Iranian influence, depleted military capacity, and lacked a consistent humanitarian-intervention principle.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: Without transcendent authority, atheism provides no binding reason why moral requirements must govern conduct rather than remain matters of individual preference.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-02.proposition: If the universe exhibits origin, order, and eternal law, seeking the source and governing human conduct by that law is reasonable, while expelling divine authority risks deifying destructive human rulers.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: The binding of Isaac repudiates rather than endorses human sacrifice, while Christianity redirects preexisting destructive impulses and offers atonement and hope for grievous wrongdoing.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: Recognizing moral rules does not establish their authority, so atheists who affirm objective right and wrong rely on a religious moral inheritance without supplying an equivalent secular foundation.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-04.proposition: Launching an aggressive war is morally and logically different from refraining from war, so treating intervention and nonintervention as equivalently imperial obscures the aggressor's distinct burden.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-08.proposition: Although human beings can dangerously misunderstand religion and commit wickedness, religious belief has produced more good than harm and its abandonment threatens civilizational order.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-10.proposition: The French Revolutionary Terror and the avowedly anti-religious Soviet system show that secular ideological power can produce mass persecution, making it evasive to redescribe Soviet atheism as religion.
